hypothesis: The project's hypothesis: a capability leaves a recurring difference between the traces of correct and wrong answers, and editing the weights where that recurring difference lives repairs the capability. This run reads where it lives for the one decision the chain is built on, in the model that changed that decision most.
why_this_direction: Step 3 asks for the discrepancy along the whole path, and where it appears is reported, not chosen. The chain declared in runs/sign-chain-29-34-original edits feed-forward 29 to 34 because, in the ORIGINAL, those six merges together write the descent's sign margin (records/development/2026-11-12-path-forward/README.md, sign-direct). That finding says where the sign is written in the unedited model; it does not say whether the six are where the difference lives or only where an upstream difference is transcribed. One model on disk separates the two: a2-path changed 18 matrices at layers 0 to 8 and nothing at 29 to 34, and answering on its own it adds the descent in 29 of the 30 answers that subtracted it (ROUND-2.md, Status). If its unedited late six write the plus from the state that reaches them, the difference at the sign is already present upstream of the chain's site and an upstream correction is a second route to the same decision; if they still write the minus and the plus comes from elsewhere, the late six are not a pure transcriber and the chain's site carries the decision itself. Either reading changes what the chain's result means and what a competing construction should be, and it needs no solve: one own-answer capture on a card that is idle.
repeating_pattern_check: Three things have happened more than once. (1) A count of answers that changed a token was taken for a repaired computation: a2-path's 29 of 30, correction-at-19's fifteen conditional sign margins, B's six repairs, each later qualified by a changed opening or history (ROUND-2.md: correction-at-19 changes its opening at the third token in 26 of 30 histories; a2-path leaves the original text at the fourth token). Why it keeps happening: the model's own text differs from the recordings' before the decision row, so weights and history are confounded in every own answer. This run separates them at the decision row itself: the original's weights read the same tokens (the control), so at one row on one text the only difference is the weights. (2) A finding on the original was carried to an edited model as if the same merges did the same thing there (the given-text readings that did not predict own answers, November 10). This run reads the edited model's own path and takes no row from the original's offsets. (3) Work proceeded one construction at a time with a card idle (Marcos, November 12). This run uses card 1 while the chain uses card 0 and waits for nothing of the chain's.
what_went_wrong_before: Every construction so far repaired some answers and broke others, and each was read after the fact with instruments built for it. The sign-direct instrument was laid on the original's own answers and the twelve counterexamples only (39 rows); no edited model's own path has been read with it, so the claim that the late chain is the place of the sign rests on the unedited model alone.
rule: Data roles as the owner set them: the thirty fitting questions (15 wrong, 15 correct) of controlled-bf16-4's cohort only. The no-fit 15 + 15 are not read and reserved-40b stays sealed. This reading selects no candidate, sets no target, scores no answer as repaired and feeds no solve: a changed sign is not a repaired computation (Astra's reading contract, section 5). Rows are found on each path from its own text; after two texts' first differing token their rows are shown side by side, never paired by offset. The model files are only read.

prediction: Stated before any pass. (1) Among the fifteen fitting wrong questions, a2-path's own answer joins the initial kinetic energy to the descent with a plus in most of those whose original answer has a minus there; the count is reported with every answer that has no such row named as a gap. (2) The route: at each such plus row of a2-path's own path, the summed direct term of the late six to score(' -') - score(' +') is negative (it favours the plus), although none of the six was changed, and it is larger in size than the summed direct term of the edited layers 0 to 8. That is, the six that write the minus in the original write the plus from what a2-path's early matrices pass on. (3) Weights, not history: with the original's weights reading a2-path's own tokens up to that row, the margin at the same step favours the minus in most of these answers, so the plus is made by the changed weights on that text and not by the rewording before it.
would_weaken_it: Of (2): a late-six sum that stays positive at a2-path's plus rows, with the plus written by other merges, says the six are not transcribing an upstream state there and that the early edit reaches the sign by another path; then the chain's site is not shown to carry the decision in an edited model. Of (3): the original's weights also favouring the plus on a2-path's text in most answers says the flip is carried by the reworded history, so a2-path's 29 of 30 counts a rewording and not a changed computation at the sign, and a count of plus signs on own answers is not evidence that weights changed the decision (the token is then shown, on this model, not to define the divergence). Of (1): few plus rows among the fitting fifteen leaves too few rows to read (2) and (3), and the run says so rather than pooling other rows in.
